name: Awesome DESIGN.md
summary: A collection of DESIGN.md files analysing popular brand design systems. Drop one into your project and let coding agents generate a matching UI.

agent_entrypoints.what: The full design-language document for one brand: palette, type scale, spacing, component rules. This is the payload - read it before writing any UI.
Short human summary of that brand's design language.
The categorised index of every available brand. Read it to resolve a vague style request to a concrete brand slug.
Authoritative list of brand slugs currently in the repo - more reliable than the README when it lags.

use_when: Someone describes the look they want by naming a company ('make it feel like Linear').
You need a written design language before generating screens, so output stays consistent across a session.
You are seeding a new project and want a defensible starting palette and type scale.
avoid_when: You need runnable components - these are documents, not code.
The work is a public-facing product that would be mistaken for the analysed brand. Borrow the system, not the identity.

notes: The DESIGN.md files describe real companies' visual systems. Use them as craft references and starting points. Do not reproduce another company's logo, wordmark, or trade dress in shipped work.
